# Composites West, Inc.

> Composites West is a carbon fiber and advanced composites "reinforcement boutique" founded in 2001, based in Reno, Nevada, USA. The company supplies the highest-quality composite reinforcement materials it can source, serving aerospace, marine, automotive, sporting goods, civil engineering/infrastructure, and industrial markets. Pricing is quote-based: call (775) 833-4300 or email info@compositeswest.com.

Key facts:
- Specialties: carbon fiber fabric reinforcements — woven (plain, twill, satin), non-crimp ±45° knits, unidirectional, and braid — plus fiberglass, prepregs, honeycomb core, vacuum bagging and infusion materials.
- Fibers include high modulus (HR40), intermediate modulus, and 1K/3K/6K/12K standard modulus carbon.
- Brands: Hexcel, Toray, FCIM, CFA.
- The Hex-3R product line is a complete FRP structural strengthening system for concrete repair and seismic retrofit: carbon/glass wraps, matched structural epoxies, FireLam fire-protection coatings, and FibrAnchor shear anchors.

## How to choose a carbon fiber fabric

Four properties decide almost every selection, in this order:

1. **Fiber type / modulus** — standard modulus (T300-class) covers most work; intermediate and high modulus (HR40) are used when a part is stiffness-limited rather than strength-limited.
2. **Areal weight** — given in oz/yd² and gsm (multiply oz/yd² by ~33.9 for gsm). Lighter fabric gives finer thickness control and better drape; heavier fabric builds structure in fewer plies.
3. **Construction** — plain weave (most stable, least drape), 2×2 twill (balanced, the cosmetic carbon look), 8-harness satin (best drape, lowest crimp, for compound curves), unidirectional (zero crimp, maximum stiffness along one axis), ±45° non-crimp knit (torsional and shear stiffness).
4. **Roll width** — determines whether a part is covered without seams. Widths include 12″, 25″, 50″, and 60″.

- [About](https://compositeswest.com/about/): Company history and markets served

- [Aerospace](https://compositeswest.com/applications/aerospace/): High and intermediate modulus carbon, satin and twill for structure and tooling
- [Marine](https://compositeswest.com/applications/marine/): ±45° non-crimp knits for torsional stiffness in masts, hulls, and foils
- [Infrastructure](https://compositeswest.com/applications/infrastructure/): FRP structural strengthening and seismic retrofit of concrete and masonry
- [Sporting Goods](https://compositeswest.com/applications/sporting-goods/): Tuned stiffness for bicycles, skis, racquets, and prosthetics
- [Automotive](https://compositeswest.com/applications/automotive/): 2×2 twill for cosmetic body panels and structural components
- [Material Finder](https://compositeswest.com/material-finder/): Interactive tool — answer four questions about part geometry, load direction, design priority, and part size to get every fabric ranked with reasoning and trade-offs. Results are shareable via URL, e.g. `/material-finder/?geometry=compound&load=torsion&priority=stiff&size=large`
